recommendations.headline: Only 18% of calls convert to an order, and conversion is driven far more by how satisfied the customer is with the call (71% win rate when satisfied vs just 2% when dissatisfied) than by price alone, since 68% of calls (2,259) never even discuss price.
behaviour: Price comparison dominates conversations: price_enquiry is the top intent (1,107 calls, 33%), 670 customers are tagged price_shopper and 398 are comparing_quotes, yet price_high objection still only wins 22% of the time.
Most calls end undecided: 1,842 of 3,326 calls (55%) close as 'callback' vs just 591 as 'order', showing a heavy backlog of unresolved follow-ups.
Stock availability is the #1 practical blocker: 614 customers need stock_availability info and 528 raise it as an objection, with only a 16% win rate on those calls.
Dealers generate the most volume (1,725 calls, 52%) but convert below fabricators (31% vs 36% win rate); the 821 'unknown' segment calls convert worst at only 15%.
Reps frequently miss basic sales discipline: 620 calls have no fixed follow-up set, 548 show slow/unclear answers, and 343 never had a quote sent at all.
satisfaction: Only 29% of calls (971) end with the customer satisfied, 56% (1,854) are neutral and 10% (318) dissatisfied - and satisfaction is the single biggest driver of outcome (71% vs 10% vs 2% win rates respectively).

Price is rarely the explicit dealbreaker: 2,259 calls (68%) never reach a price discussion, and when price is discussed, 274 accept vs only 127 call it too high - most lost deals are about service, stock or follow-through, not price.

Negative sentiment (572 calls, 17%) outweighs positive sentiment (353, 11%), suggesting room to improve overall call experience, especially given satisfied customers convert 7x better than neutral ones.

conversion.title: Fix follow-up discipline
conversion.evidence: 620 calls had no fixed follow-up set and 1,842 calls (55%) end as 'callback'; neutral-satisfaction calls convert at only 10% vs 71% when satisfied.
conversion.action: Make every call end with a concrete next step (date/time/channel) logged in CRM; manager to audit callback calls weekly for closure.

conversion.title: Send quotes same-day
conversion.evidence: 343 calls had no quote sent despite price_enquiry being the top intent (1,107 calls, 33%).
conversion.action: Set an SLA that every price enquiry gets a written quote via WhatsApp/email within a few hours, with confirmation of receipt.

conversion.title: Offer alternatives when stock is short
conversion.evidence: Stock_availability is the top objection (528 calls, only 16% win) and 249 calls show reps didn't offer an alternative.
conversion.action: Train reps to immediately propose nearest size/brand/location substitute instead of a flat 'not available' response; give reps a live multi-location stock view.

conversion.title: Always ask for the order
conversion.evidence: 236 calls show reps never asked for the order, while overall order conversion is just 18%.
conversion.action: Coach reps to explicitly request a PO/confirmation at the end of every qualified call, not just share information.

conversion.title: Qualify and tag segment early
conversion.evidence: 821 'unknown' segment calls convert at only 15% vs 31-40% for identified segments (dealer, fabricator, end_user).
conversion.action: Make segment capture (dealer/fabricator/contractor/etc.) a mandatory first-two-minutes step so the right pitch and follow-up track is used.

conversion.title: Reduce unclear/slow responses
conversion.evidence: 548 calls flagged slow_or_unclear_answer, especially on technical and credit questions (needs_technical_help 417, credit_terms objection 150 at 15% win).
conversion.action: Create a one-page rate/spec/credit-policy quick-reference for reps to answer confidently without placing customers on long hold.

conversion.title: Reframe competitor-price conversations
conversion.evidence: Competitor_cheaper objection has the lowest win rate of all objections (10%, 144 calls) and JSW is cited most often among 50 competitor mentions.
conversion.action: Equip reps with a short value script (certification, cutting service, delivery reliability) to use before considering any price move.

offers.for_whom: Fabricators and contractors needing custom lengths
offers.why: 314 calls flag cutting_processing as a need, and several successful calls closed specifically around cutting/bending arrangements.

offers.title: Guaranteed fast/site delivery slots
offers.why: 560 calls need fast_delivery and 172 need site_delivery; delivery_time is a top-4 objection (221 calls).

offers.why: 437 calls need regular_updates and most price enquiries ask for rates to be sent via WhatsApp/email.

offers.title: Standard test-certificate bundling
offers.why: 209 calls need test_certificate and several lost/delayed calls cite missing or late TC as the sticking point.

offers.title: Evaluate structured credit period for vetted repeat buyers
offers.for_whom: Repeat/bulk buyers with consistent payment history
offers.why: 174 customers show needs_credit behaviour and 134 cite credit_period need, though credit_terms objection only wins 15% currently - needs a clear policy, not ad hoc promises.

offers.title: Small-quantity/split-load service
offers.why: 46 calls need small_quantity and min_quantity objection (74 calls) only wins 20% currently.

loyalty.title: Repeat-buyer recognition tier
loyalty.how: Flag repeat_buyer accounts in CRM and give them priority stock allocation and faster callback SLAs.
loyalty.why: 308 calls are tagged repeat_buyer but only 15 are tagged loyal_to_us - a large untapped base to formalize.

loyalty.title: Named account manager for top dealers
loyalty.how: Assign a single point of contact per key dealer account, visible to the customer.
loyalty.why: Customers repeatedly ask 'who is handling our account?' and 620 calls show no fixed follow-up, indicating ownership gaps.

loyalty.title: Proactive dispatch/status updates
loyalty.how: Automate WhatsApp/SMS alerts at order confirmation, loading, and dispatch stages without customer having to ask.
loyalty.why: 437 calls need regular_updates and many customer questions are reactive follow-ups like 'has the vehicle arrived?'.

loyalty.title: Referral recognition program
loyalty.how: Acknowledge and prioritize customers who refer others with faster service, not discounts.
loyalty.why: Only 22 calls show referral behaviour currently - a low base that could grow with simple recognition.

loyalty.title: Priority queue for bulk/urgent orders
loyalty.how: Create a fast-track loading/dispatch lane for bulk_buyer and urgent_buyer tagged accounts.
loyalty.why: 373 bulk_buyer and 327 urgent_buyer calls show these segments value speed, which can build loyalty without price cuts.

top_questions.answer_tip: Confirm you will send a written quote via WhatsApp/email within a fixed short window and state its validity period.

top_questions.answer_tip: Check live multi-location stock and offer the closest available alternative immediately if the exact item is short.

recommendations.headline: Varsha's biggest gap is call execution, not price: 70% of calls (1,862) never even get to a price discussion, yet 57% end neutral with only a 10% win rate (vs 72% when satisfied) - driven mainly by 505 calls with no fixed follow-up and 461 slow/unclear answers.
behaviour: Most calls stall rather than close: callback is the outcome in 1,481 of 2,671 calls (55%) vs only 486 orders (18%).
Stock availability is both the top need (487 mentions) and top objection (436 cases, only 17% win rate), showing customers frequently can't get a clear stock answer.
Price shopping is widespread - price_shopper (491) and comparing_quotes (291) behaviours, plus price_high objection in 434 calls - but price is only formally discussed in 809 of 2,671 calls (30%).
Repeat buyers (251 calls) and dealers (1,345 calls) are the core base, but dealer win rate is just 31% and only 13 calls show customers explicitly 'loyal_to_us'.
Bulk (281) and urgent (276) buyers are sizable, time-sensitive segments that need quick, decisive handling.
satisfaction: Satisfaction directly drives sales: win rate is 72% when satisfied (757 calls) vs 10% when neutral (1,516 calls) and just 3% when dissatisfied (278 calls).
57% of all calls (1,516) end in a neutral mood - this is the single largest pool of lost potential given the 10% conversion rate there.
Price is rarely a dealbreaker when discussed: of calls where price was raised, 205 accepted and 501 negotiated, vs only 103 'too high' - most price objections are workable if value is explained.
Credit terms and competitor-cheaper objections convert worst (13% and 9% win rate respectively), suggesting these need a non-price response, not a discount reflex.

conversion.title: Always fix a concrete next step before hanging up
conversion.evidence: no_follow_up_fixed is the #1 rep-missed issue in 505 calls (19%), and 55% of calls end as 'callback' with no order.
conversion.action: End every call with a specific date/time and action (e.g., 'I will send quote by 5pm, you confirm by tomorrow 11am') and log it.

conversion.evidence: 461 calls flagged as slow_or_unclear_answer; stock_availability objection alone appears 436 times with only 17% win rate.
conversion.action: Check live stock/price before or at start of call; if unsure, commit to a callback within a fixed short window (e.g., 15 minutes) instead of leaving it open.

conversion.title: Send a written quote on every pricing call, same day
conversion.evidence: 290 calls had no_quote_sent; 'not_discussed' price status covers 70% of calls.
conversion.action: Follow every price_enquiry or order call with a WhatsApp/email quote within the same session, even if verbal rate was given.

conversion.title: Offer an alternative when the exact item/size is unavailable

conversion.action: When the exact size/brand is out of stock, proactively suggest nearest available size, alternate brand, or part-shipment instead of just saying 'not available'.

conversion.title: Explicitly ask for the order at the end of promising calls

conversion.action: After addressing the need, directly ask 'Shall I book this order / shall I send the vehicle?' instead of leaving it open-ended.

conversion.title: Lead with value before quoting price

conversion.action: Mention test certificate, cutting service, and stock reliability before stating the rate, so price is heard in context.

conversion.title: Clarify full requirement upfront to avoid rework
conversion.evidence: didnt_ask_requirement missed in 66 calls; summaries show mismatches (e.g., customer got 3mm instead of 8mm).
conversion.action: Confirm grade, size, quantity, and delivery location in one go at call start before quoting or booking.

recommendations.headline: Venkatesh's calls convert at only 16% and win-rate collapses from 65% (satisfied) to 9% (neutral) because he fails to fix a follow-up (115 calls) or ask for the order (66 calls) more often than any price issue.
behaviour: Customers are heavily price-driven: 179 are tagged price_shopper and 107 comparing_quotes, with price_high the top objection (134 calls, 20%).
Most calls end non-committally: 361 of 655 (55%) outcomes are 'callback' and only 105 (16%) become orders.
Large base of repeat/bulk business exists (92 bulk_buyer, 57 repeat_buyer) but loyal_to_us is tagged only twice - loyalty isn't being reinforced on calls.
Stock availability is both the top stated need (127) and a major objection (92 calls) with just 13% win rate when raised.
Urgency is mostly medium (404) or low (144) - only 82 are high urgency, so most customers can be converted with good follow-up rather than reacting to pressure.
satisfaction: Only 214/655 calls (33%) leave customers satisfied; 338 (52%) are rated neutral and 40 (6%) dissatisfied.
Satisfaction is the strongest predictor of sales: satisfied calls win 65% of the time vs just 9% for neutral and 0% for dissatisfied - far bigger swing than any price variable.
Price is often left unresolved: in 397 of 655 calls (61%) price_reaction is 'not_discussed', yet 134 calls still raise price_high as an objection - price is parked, not actually closed.
When price is negotiated, outcomes are reasonable (165 calls negotiating, 69 accepted, only 24 too_high) - the price itself is less often the blocker than how the call is handled.
